result.title: Is This 3D Asset Usable? Beyond the Beauty Render for Asset Curation
result.summary: Large 3D repositories make it easy to collect assets, but difficult to determine whether they can be reused reliably across scene assembly, editing, rendering, game production, and training-data construction. An asset can look plausible in RGB while hiding disconnected geometry, problematic UV organization, or materials that fail to resolve correctly after import. We introduce Diagnostic Rendered Evidence (DRE): aligned beauty, wireframe, and UV-seam-plus-wireframe views scored by pass-specific frozen ViT classifiers and combined through late fusion. On 1,234 human labeled TexVerse assets, nested grouped evaluation achieves 86.36% balanced accuracy and 88.32% bad-asset recall. On a separate, balanced 764 external reference test, DRE achieved 88.9% balanced reference-label accuracy. Our method requires only an imported asset and renderer-derived evidence, without repository identity, creator, popularity, text, or source metadata at inference. Our results support cross-corpus portability and show that purpose built diagnostic views expose defects that just the beauty views can miss. Webpage: https://rbz-99.github.io/is-this-3d-asset-usable/

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究「3D 资产是否可用」的判定问题，提出 Diagnostic Rendered Evidence：将对齐的 beauty、wireframe、UV 缝线加线框三种视图分别送入专用的冻结 ViT 分类器，再以晚期融合给出可用性判断，并在人工标注的 TexVerse 子集与外部平衡测试集上验证跨语料可迁移性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心发现「仅靠 beauty 视图会漏掉缺陷、需补充诊断性视图」与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、多源证据组合的评价思路可能相通，可供核查诊断视图的设计与融合方式能否迁移到 VLM 的证据取舍与停止决策，但论文不涉及 latent 推理或生成过程。
